title: Product-name validation accepts a missing or non-string product
description:
Bug found reviewing PR #42 (merged e0dd639). PRODUCT_NAME_PATTERN.test(value) coerces its argument to a string, so a product that is undefined (missing) becomes "undefined" and matches /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$/. A one-element array such as ["cyclotron"] also coerces to "cyclotron" and passes, and the same coercion lets an array-wrapped issuer pass the issuer pattern.

Affected: registrationRules (accounts/registration.ts) for product and issuer, grantRules (accounts/operator-policy.ts) for product and issuer, and the PRODUCT_NAME_PATTERN.test in setEntitlement (accounts/durable-accounts.ts). siteEntryRules (accounts/papyrus-sites.ts) already has a string rule before its pattern rule and is not affected.

Impact: registrations and operator grants are deployment-owned configs validated at startup. No request-supplied data reaches these validators, and the committed deployment configs have valid string products, so nothing reachable in production hits this today. It could only admit a deployment-config mistake (a registration or grant with no product, stored as undefined). setEntitlement receives its product from the registered-product list (matched by route), not from the request body, so it is not reachable either; it is hardened for consistency.

Design note: the literal string "undefined" is a legitimate product name by the pattern (lowercase letters), so it stays accepted; the typeof rule is what rejects a missing product.

Acceptance criteria:
- Registration, operator grant and Papyrus site validators reject a missing, null, numeric and array-wrapped product with a specific "must be a string" message and unchanged status and error codes.
- The same for issuer on registrations and operator grants.
- setEntitlement rejects a non-string product with the existing 400 invalid_entitlement.
- A shared isProductName type guard is used by every product-name check.
- Committed deployment configs still validate; lint, typecheck, tests pass.
